stances_toward.note: No recognition (the dataset row says so) but unusually close ties built since Vystrcil's August 2020 visit: direct Taipei-Prague flights (2023), a CzechInvest office in Taipei (2024), a Czech Centre. Cooling because the Babiš cabinet refused a government aircraft for the Senate president's April 2026 trip; Hala's analysis calls the shift 'real, but shallow' and the institutional links intact. Bond - affinity: democratic kinship, Senate and Pavel's channel.

stances_toward.note: Lithuania does not recognise Taiwan (a dataset row records that) but hosts the Taiwanese Representative Office and trades EUR 191m (2025, from EUR 111m in 2021); Taiwanese direct investment rose from EUR 0.53m (2021) to EUR 7.21m (2024). Partner and not ally: this is transactional cooperation with no alignment, and Vilnius is now negotiating a normalisation that may cost the office its name. The president says Lithuania wants to balance the two. Bond - affinity: shared experience of a larger neighbour.

stances_toward.note: No diplomatic relations: Latvia follows the One China line but has hosted a Taipei Mission in Riga since 1992 (it moved to Ausekla iela in 2021) and 18 of 100 deputies sit in the Latvia-Taiwan friendship group; in Aug 2025 Taiwan's deputy speaker suggested Latvia open an office in Taiwan, a proposal only. Partner as the transactional, non-aligned grade; the exit from 16+1 in 2022 is the context. Cooperation is low-cost and the trend is stable. Bond - affinity: both are small democracies in the shadow of a larger neighbour.
